newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- supply, data worries takeover.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- supply, data worries takeover.

text.p: The U.S. municipal market ignored a Treasury rally Monday, worried about a large slate of new issues and a raft of economic data on tap this week.
Traders said prices remained unchanged on the day, despite a 20/32 rise in the Treasury long bond, whose yield dropped to 6.41 percent.
"I think dealers' inventories are probably a little bit higher than they had been and I think that's putting a lid on the couple of things that have been out for the bid," one trader said.

The calendar on Monday grew by another $640 million, after Lehman Brothers said it would price the week's largest negotiated offering on Thursday, a $640 million Arapahoe County, Colo., deal for the E-470 Public Highway project.
The deal, which will carry insurance from MBIA Insurance Corp, is the largest of the $3.6 billion in deals expected for the week, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Tuesday's calendar totaled $1.1 billion in 40 sales.
Negotiated offerings total $700 million in 22 sales, with a $159 million Massachusetts Port Authority offering through Bear, Stearns & Co., Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 18 sales totaling $397 million are scheduled for Tuesday. A 215 million Minnesota offering at 1100 EDT is the largest.

Among the week's more closely-watched data will be the Employment Cost Index, a key indicator of inflation, which was set for release Tuesday. Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the figure to show a 0.8 percent increase.

The week's other main focus, the payrolls data for July, were due out Friday. Predictions are for a 193,000 rise, down from the previous month's 217,000. The unemployment rate was predicted at 4.9 percent, down from 5.0 percent.

In Chicago futures markets Monday, September municipal bonds rose 11/32 to 121-1/32, while September Treasury bonds gained 13/32 to 115-14/32. The MOB sread between the two contracts narrowed to 179 ticks from 181 ticks at the close on Friday.
In the secondary market, bids on Atlanta FGIC 5-1/4 water and sewer bonds of 2027 were unchanged at 5.37 percent.
Florida Ports Financing Commission MBIA 5-3/8s of 2027 were bid at 5.49 percent, one basis point below Friday's closing bid.
